turns.t: Doctor, I'm Hannah, Greg's wife. He won't say it, so I will: I'm worried about how much he's drinking.
Hannah, I'm fine. It's a glass of wine in the evenings. ~
Greg, I'd like to hear from you first. How much do you drink in a typical day?
A bottle of wine, give or take. Maybe a bit more at weekends.
It's more than that. There's a bottle every night, and he's started before lunch on his days off.
Thank you both. When did the drinking go up, would you say?
I don't know. Gradually. Since I changed jobs, I think. Or maybe before.
It's the last year, I think, but I honestly couldn't say when it tipped over.
How are your mornings?
Shaky. My hands tremble. I settle down after a coffee.
And he's sweaty and irritable until he has a drink at lunchtime.
How's your sleep?
Poor. I fall asleep fine, and wake at three, and lie there.
And how's your mood?
A bit flat. And anxious, that's the word.
Any thoughts of harming yourself?
No. No, not at all.
Any tablets at the moment?
Just a vitamin B tablet, thiamine, 100 mg, once a day, that Hannah makes me take.
Good. Any allergies to medicines or anything else?
No. I'm not allergic to anything.
He reacted to codeine once, Greg, you came out in hives, and your face swelled. It was years ago, before we married.
I'll note that you say no allergies and Hannah recalls a reaction to codeine, and I'll record both. Any health conditions?
High blood pressure, an ulcer a few years ago, and I had some depression, a while back.
Let me check you. Pulse, pressure, temperature. ~
Go on. ~
Pulse 92, blood pressure 150 over 94, temperature 36.8, oxygen 98 percent, weight 94 kilos.
That's high, isn't it? ~
The pressure and pulse are up, which fits with the alcohol and the morning shakes. Any breathlessness, chest pain?
No. Nothing.
Greg, from what you and Hannah describe, drinking a bottle of wine or more daily, shakes in the morning and drinking to settle them, this looks like harmful alcohol use with early dependence.
Dependence. That's a strong word. ~
It's a medical description, and it's treatable. And it's good that you've come. ~
Can he stop on his own? ~
Please don't stop suddenly, because with this level of drinking, withdrawal can be dangerous. We'll plan it safely.
What does that involve? ~
I'd like to refer you to the community alcohol service, and I'd like to arrange blood tests, for your liver and blood count, today.
Right. ~
Keep taking the thiamine, eat regular meals, and don't drive after drinking.
I'll keep an eye on him. ~
I'd like to see you again in a week. If you get severe shakes, confusion, hallucinations, or a fit, go to the emergency department.
Okay. Thank you. ~
